item.title: Sampling Distribution of Mean Bag Weight
item.stimulus: A packaging line fills bags of rice. The weight of a bag is normally distributed with a mean of 1000 grams and a standard deviation of 24 grams. A quality inspector will weigh a random sample of bags taken from the thousands filled today.

parts.prompt: Find the mean and the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean x̄ for random samples of 16 bags.

criteria.text: States that the mean of the sampling distribution of x̄ is μ = 1000 grams.
criteria.evidence: Response gives 1000 grams as the mean of the sampling distribution of the sample mean.
criteria.fix: The sampling distribution of x̄ is centered at the population mean, whatever the sample size; state that value with units.

criteria.text: Calculates the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of x̄ as σ/√n = 24/√16 = 6 grams.
criteria.evidence: Response divides 24 by √16 and reports about 6 grams.
criteria.fix: Divide the population standard deviation by the square root of the sample size, and keep the units.

parts.prompt: Is the sampling distribution of x̄ approximately normal? Justify your answer by checking the conditions.

criteria.text: States that the sampling distribution of x̄ is approximately normal because the sample is random and much smaller than 10% of all bags, so the values are independent, and the population of bag weights is normally distributed, so x̄ is normal for any sample size.
criteria.evidence: Response says the sampling distribution is approximately normal and gives the reason: random sample, independence, and a normal population.
criteria.fix: Justify normality with a normal population or with sample sizes of at least 30 (central limit theorem), and check independence.

parts.prompt: Find the probability that the mean of a random sample of 16 bags is greater than 1005 grams.

criteria.text: Finds the probability that the mean of a random sample of 16 bags is greater than 1005 grams: the probability is about 0.2023, using a normal distribution with mean 1000 and standard deviation 6 (for example, z = (1005 − 1000)/6 = 0.83).
criteria.evidence: Response uses the mean 1000 and standard deviation 6 of the sampling distribution (not of single values), by a z-score or a direct normal calculation, and reports about 0.2023.
criteria.fix: Use the standard deviation of the sample mean, not of single values, then find the normal area in the stated direction.

parts.prompt: Suppose the sample size is 64 instead of 16. How does the standard deviation of x̄ change? Give its new value.

criteria.text: States that with n = 64 the standard deviation of the sampling distribution becomes 3 grams, smaller than 6 grams, because σ/√n decreases as n increases.
criteria.evidence: Response gives 3 grams for the new sample size and says the standard deviation decreases as n increases.
criteria.fix: Substitute the new sample size into σ/√n; larger samples give a smaller standard deviation of x̄.

item.model_answer:
(a) The mean of the sampling distribution of x̄ is μ = 1000 grams. The standard deviation is σ/√n = 24/√16 = 6 grams.

(b) Yes. The sampling distribution of x̄ is approximately normal because the sample is random and much smaller than 10% of all bags, so the values are independent, and the population of bag weights is normally distributed, so x̄ is normal for any sample size.

(c) z = (1005 − 1000)/6 = 0.83, so the probability that x̄ is greater than 1005 grams is about 0.2023.

(d) With n = 64, the standard deviation of x̄ is 24/√64 = 3 grams, smaller than 6 grams, because σ/√n decreases as n increases.

parts.prompt: For 95% confidence, the critical value from the standard normal distribution is z* = 1.96, which is smaller than t* = 2.131. Explain why t* is larger.

criteria.text: States that t* = 2.131 is larger than the normal critical value z* = 1.96 for 95% confidence, because the t-distribution (with 15 degrees of freedom) has heavier tails than the normal distribution.

item.title: Test of Mean Commute Difference Between Two Routes
item.stimulus: A commuter randomly selected 12 drivers from a large company, and each drove both route A and route B in a random order. For each driver, the difference (route A time minus route B time) in minutes was calculated. The sample of differences has mean −2.9 minutes and standard deviation 5.1 minutes, with no strong skewness and no outliers. The commuter tests H₀: μ_d = 0 versus Hₐ: μ_d ≠ 0 at significance level α = 0.05, where μ_d is the population mean difference (route A minus route B). Technology gives a p-value of 0.0746.

parts.prompt: Calculate the test statistic.

criteria.text: Calculates the test statistic t = d̄/(s_d/√n) = −2.90/(5.1/√12) = −1.97.
criteria.evidence: Response substitutes the sample values into the formula and reports t of about −1.97.
criteria.fix: Subtract the null value from the sample statistic and divide by the standard error computed from the sample standard deviations.

parts.prompt: Interpret the p-value in context.

criteria.text: Interprets the p-value 0.0746: assuming the mean commute-time difference (route A minus route B) for all drivers is 0, the probability of getting a sample mean difference at least 2.9 minutes away from 0 in either direction (equivalently, a test statistic at least about 1.97 away from 0) is about 0.0746.
criteria.evidence: Response says 0.0746 is the probability, computed assuming the mean commute-time difference (route A minus route B) for all drivers is 0, of getting a sample mean difference at least 2.9 minutes away from 0 in either direction (equivalently, a test statistic at least about 1.97 away from 0) (an equivalent statement in terms of the test statistic is also acceptable).
criteria.fix: Say the p-value is the probability of a result this extreme or more, in the direction of Hₐ, assuming H₀ is true.

parts.prompt: Use the p-value and the significance level α = 0.05 to state a conclusion about the claim, in context.

criteria.text: Compares the p-value 0.0746 with α = 0.05: because the p-value is greater than α, fail to reject H₀.
criteria.evidence: Response compares 0.0746 with 0.05, and says fail to reject H₀.
criteria.fix: Compare the p-value with α: reject H₀ when the p-value is less than or equal to α, otherwise fail to reject.

criteria.text: Concludes in context: there is not convincing evidence that the mean commute-time difference (route A minus route B) is not 0 minutes for all drivers like these.
criteria.evidence: Response states not convincing evidence for Hₐ, in terms of Hₐ and in context.
criteria.fix: State the conclusion in terms of Hₐ in context, using 'convincing evidence' or 'not convincing evidence'.

item.model_answer:
(a) t = d̄/(s_d/√n) = −2.90/(5.1/√12) = −1.97, with df = 11.

(b) Assuming the mean commute-time difference (route A minus route B) for all drivers is 0, the probability of getting a sample mean difference at least 2.9 minutes away from 0 in either direction (equivalently, a test statistic at least about 1.97 away from 0) is about 0.0746.

(c) The p-value 0.0746 is greater than α = 0.05, so we fail to reject H₀. There is not convincing evidence that the mean commute-time difference (route A minus route B) is not 0 minutes for all drivers like these.

item.title: Sampling Distribution of a Difference in Mean Delivery Times

criteria.text: States that the mean of the sampling distribution of x̄₁ − x̄₂ is μ₁ − μ₂ = 5 minutes.
criteria.evidence: Response gives 5 minutes as the mean of the sampling distribution of the difference in sample means.

criteria.text: Calculates the standard deviation of x̄₁ − x̄₂ as √(σ₁²/n₁ + σ₂²/n₂) = √(10²/50 + 7²/60) = 1.678 minutes.

criteria.fix: Add the two variance-over-sample-size terms before taking the square root; do not subtract or add the standard deviations.

criteria.fix: Justify normality with a normal population or with sample sizes of at least 30 (central limit theorem), and check independence.

parts.prompt: Find the probability that the difference x̄₁ − x̄₂ is less than 2 minutes.

criteria.text: Finds the probability that x̄₁ − x̄₂ is less than 2 minutes: the probability is about 0.0369, using a normal distribution with mean 5 and standard deviation 1.678 (for example, z = (2 − 5)/1.678 = −1.79).
criteria.evidence: Response uses the mean 5 and standard deviation 1.678 of the sampling distribution (not of single values), by a z-score or a direct normal calculation, and reports about 0.0369.
criteria.fix: Use the standard deviation of the sample mean, not of single values, then find the normal area in the stated direction.

item.model_answer:
(a) The mean is μ₁ − μ₂ = 52 − 47 = 5 minutes.

(b) √(10²/50 + 7²/60) = 1.678 minutes.

(c) Yes. The sampling distribution of x̄₁ − x̄₂ is approximately normal because both samples are random and independent, and both sample sizes (50 and 60) are at least 30.

item.title: Test of a Difference in Mean Recovery Times for Two Treatments
item.stimulus: A physiotherapy clinic randomly assigned patients to treatment 1 (26 patients, mean recovery time 71.4 minutes, standard deviation 9.8) or treatment 2 (28 patients, mean recovery time 68.9 minutes, standard deviation 11.3). Both samples have no strong skewness and no outliers. The clinic tests H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0 versus Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ ≠ 0 at significance level α = 0.05. Technology gives df ≈ 51.8 and a p-value of 0.3882.

parts.prompt: Calculate the test statistic.

criteria.text: Calculates the test statistic t = (x̄₁ − x̄₂)/√(s₁²/n₁ + s₂²/n₂) = (71.4 − 68.9)/√(9.8²/26 + 11.3²/28) = 0.87.
criteria.evidence: Response substitutes the sample values into the formula and reports t of about 0.87.
criteria.fix: Subtract the null value from the sample statistic and divide by the standard error computed from the sample standard deviations.

parts.prompt: Interpret the p-value in context.

criteria.text: Interprets the p-value 0.3882: assuming the two treatments have the same mean recovery time (μ₁ − μ₂ = 0), the probability of getting a difference in sample means at least 2.5 minutes away from 0 in either direction (equivalently, a test statistic at least about 0.87 away from 0) is about 0.3882.
criteria.evidence: Response says 0.3882 is the probability, computed assuming the two treatments have the same mean recovery time (μ₁ − μ₂ = 0), of getting a difference in sample means at least 2.5 minutes away from 0 in either direction (equivalently, a test statistic at least about 0.87 away from 0) (an equivalent statement in terms of the test statistic is also acceptable).
criteria.fix: Say the p-value is the probability of a result this extreme or more, in the direction of Hₐ, assuming H₀ is true.

parts.prompt: Use the p-value and the significance level α = 0.05 to state a conclusion about the claim, in context.

criteria.text: Compares the p-value 0.3882 with α = 0.05: because the p-value is greater than α, fail to reject H₀.
criteria.evidence: Response compares 0.3882 with 0.05, and says fail to reject H₀.
criteria.fix: Compare the p-value with α: reject H₀ when the p-value is less than or equal to α, otherwise fail to reject.

criteria.text: Concludes in context: there is not convincing evidence that the mean recovery time with treatment 1 differs from the mean recovery time with treatment 2 for the patients in this study.
criteria.evidence: Response states not convincing evidence for Hₐ, in terms of Hₐ and in context.
criteria.fix: State the conclusion in terms of Hₐ in context, using 'convincing evidence' or 'not convincing evidence'.

item.model_answer:
(a) t = (71.4 − 68.9)/√(9.8²/26 + 11.3²/28) = 0.87.

(b) Assuming the two treatments have the same mean recovery time (μ₁ − μ₂ = 0), the probability of getting a difference in sample means at least 2.5 minutes away from 0 in either direction (equivalently, a test statistic at least about 0.87 away from 0) is about 0.3882.

(c) The p-value 0.3882 is greater than α = 0.05, so we fail to reject H₀. There is not convincing evidence that the mean recovery time with treatment 1 differs from the mean recovery time with treatment 2 for the patients in this study.
